target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures report the volume of modified loans, their aging status, and the financial impact (interest rate reduction and principal forgiveness). The 2024 disclosure (bac_2024_8_D197) provides the 2024 figures ($650M modified, 0.31%, 18.89% rate reduction, $113M forgiveness) compared to the 2023 figures in the previous year's disclosure (bac_2023_8_D192: $598M modified, 0.29%).

Both disclosures monitor the performance of modified loans and report post-modification default rates and aging distributions. The 2024 disclosure (bac_2024_8_D198) explicitly compares the 2024 aging bucket details ($546M current, $58M 30-89 days, $46M >90 days) against the 2023 details ($491M current, $59M 30-89 days, $48M >90 days) referenced in the 2023 disclosure (bac_2023_8_D192).

comparisons.peer_summary: The firm may modify terms for borrowers in financial difficulty, primarily via term extensions; modified loans were mostly performing, with negligible defaults in 2024 and ~$100 million charged off in 2023 from previously modified loans.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS disclose that defaults on modified loans to borrowers in financial difficulty were insignificant or not material in 2024. BAC reports that defaults on modified credit card and other consumer loans were insignificant for both 2024 and 2023, with a total modified loan balance of $650 million at year-end 2024, of which $546 million were current and only $104 million were past due. Similarly, GS states that during 2024, loans that defaulted after being modified were not material, and substantially all remaining modified loans were performing in accordance with modified terms. However, GS notes that in 2023, it charged off approximately $100 million of previously modified loans, whereas BAC reported insignificant defaults for both years. Additionally, GS's modified loans primarily involved corporate and commercial real estate loans with term extensions, while BAC's disclosure focuses specifically on credit card and other consumer loans.

sentences.text: During 2024 and 2023, defaults of credit card and other consumer loans that had been modified within 12 months were insignificant.

At December 31, 2024, modified credit card and other consumer loans to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty over the last 12 months totaled $650 million, of which $546 million were current, $58 million were 30-89 days past due, and $46 million were greater than 90 days past due.

• During 2024, loans that defaulted after being modified were not material. During 2023, the firm charged off approximately $100 million of loans that had defaulted after being modified. Substantially all of the remaining modified loans were performing in accordance with the modified contractual terms as of both December 2024 and December 2023.
